points.description: States that linked lists are dynamic (can grow/shrink at run time), so they can store a variable number of elements, unlike fixed-size arrays.
points.partial_credit: Award about 2-3 marks for a related but incomplete statement, e.g. easy insertion/deletion or not needing contiguous memory, without mentioning variable size or dynamic nature.

rubric.notes: Give full marks if the student says in any wording that linked lists are dynamic or can change size / hold a variable number of elements. Give part marks for related advantages (e.g. easy insert/delete, no need to fix size in advance is full) that are on the right track but do not say size is flexible. Give no marks for answers unrelated to size flexibility; extra remarks do not cost marks.
